input.summary:
Terminal ileum, as you said: Stem cells and Paneth cells sit together at the crypt bases (most enriched neighbours of each other, log2 +3.7; muscle distance about 270–310 µm), which matches SI-02/SI-03. Epithelium, enteric cells and immune cells also lie where SI-01, SI-05, SI-09, SI-12 and SI-13 expect them. The problems are elsewhere:
- Stroma: "Crypt-bottom fibroblasts" lie in the submucosa (median 1,150 µm from the epithelium). "Inflammatory fibroblasts" lie against the muscle (31 µm) and lack their own markers (IL11 0%). I propose to rename both and give them the markers they actually express.
- Endothelium: "Arterial EC" (2,896 cells) are mostly capillaries (CA4/CD36/NOTCH4; GJA4 6%), so I add a Capillary EC type.
- T/NK: the NK cells carry TRDC (56%) and the IEL markers CD160/KLRC2. These are the gd intraepithelial T cells SI-08 expects, so I propose to sharpen gd T vs NK.
- Weak or unspecific markers are replaced: Enterocytes, Goblet cells, Cycling TAs, CD4 T and effector CD4, ILCs, cDC2 and Mast cells, plus negatives that the cells express (MYH11-, PDGFRA-).
- Types that are not there or not real are removed: Eosinophils (CLC in 5 cells), Follicular dendritic cells (none found) and "Naive CD4 T cells" (21 cycling cells).

edits.reason: PCLAF and UBE2C are detected in few cells; RRM2 and TYMS separate the cycling crypt cells better.
edits.evidence: PCLAF 11%, UBE2C 17% in Cycling TAs; RRM2 46% vs 5%, TYMS 41% vs 5% in siblings

edits.reason: FABP2 is not specific among epithelial cells here; APOB, MGAM and CYP3A4 mark the absorptive villus enterocytes (SI-04).
edits.evidence: FABP2 92% vs 69% in siblings; APOB 85% vs 16%, MGAM 74% vs 14%, CYP3A4 61% vs 9%

edits.reason: SPDEF is barely detected; REP15 and ITLN1 are the best goblet separators in this panel.
edits.evidence: SPDEF 8%; REP15 62% vs 13%, ITLN1 88% vs 34%, SPINK4 79% vs 26%

edits.reason: IL7R is expressed by nearly all lymphocytes (ILCs, CD8, NK), so the CD4 group marker is not specific with it.
edits.evidence: CD4|CD40LG|IL7R+ 90% in CD4 T vs 74% in siblings; IL7R 94% in ILCs

edits.reason: The 21 cells called naive do not express CCR7/SELL and are cycling cells (MKI67, TYMS, RRM2). The lamina propria holds few naive T cells.
edits.evidence: CCR7 14%, SELL 14%; MKI67 71%, TYMS 67%, RRM2 67% in these 21 cells

edits.markers: CCL5+ KLRB1+ CD69+ CD40LG+ FOXP3- CCR7-
edits.reason: These markers barely separate the type from other T cells (fold 1.05), and GZMK is weak. CD69 (tissue residency) is one of the type's top genes.
edits.evidence: GZMK 9%; CD69 47% vs 18%, CCL5 46% vs 12%

edits.reason: No cells were called gd T: the TRDC+ intraepithelial lymphocytes went to NK cells. CD160 and KLRC2 mark these IELs, which are expected in the ileal epithelium (SI-08).
edits.evidence: TRDC in 56% of 'NK cells' vs 3% of other T/NK; CD160 41% vs 4%, KLRC2 68% vs 17%; NK cells: CD3E- flagged (48% detected)

edits.markers: KLRF1+ NKG7+ KLRD1+ NCAM1+ TRDC- CD3D-
edits.reason: Keep true NK cells KLRF1+ and exclude the TRDC+ gd T cells now captured above.
edits.evidence: CD3E- negative detected in 48% of NK cells; TRDC 56%

edits.reason: IL7R is not specific among T/NK cells. RORC, KIT and IL1R1 already define ILC3s.
edits.evidence: IL7R 94% in ILCs vs 76% in siblings; RORC 69% vs 8%, KIT 77% vs 4%

edits.reason: The panel cannot detect eosinophils here: their markers are almost absent.
edits.evidence: CLC in 5 and CCR3 in 2 of 2,487 myeloid cells; type not found

edits.reason: CLEC10A alone is shared with monocytes (51%). Requiring ITGAX and excluding monocyte (FCN1) and cDC1 (CLEC9A) markers sharpens cDC2.
edits.evidence: CLEC10A 30% vs 22% in siblings; Monocytes–cDC2 confusion 0.18; ITGAX 73% vs 48%

edits.reason: CMA1 (chymase) is low in mucosal mast cells; IL1RL1 is a strong mast cell marker here.
edits.evidence: CMA1 23%; IL1RL1 85% vs 1%

edits.reason: The negative marker does not discriminate: fibroblasts next to the muscle pick up MYH11 as often as other cells do.
edits.evidence: MYH11 36% in fibroblasts vs 37% in siblings

edits.reason: PDGFRA is detected less often here than in the other fibroblasts, so it does not mark this type. BMP5 and F3 mark these subepithelial cells, which lie right under the epithelium.
edits.evidence: PDGFRA 48% vs 63% in siblings; BMP5 43% vs 2%; distance to epithelium median 0 µm

edits.reason: PDGFRA- is wrong for these cells. SFRP2 and OGN are their top genes.
edits.evidence: PDGFRA detected in 73%; SFRP2 84% vs 18%, OGN 77% vs 22%

edits.reason: These cells do not lie at the crypt bottom: they are deep, in the submucosa near muscle, neurons and macrophages.
edits.evidence: distance to epithelium median 1,150 µm (IQR 721–1,632), to muscle 127 µm

edits.reason: The inflammatory markers are essentially absent. These cells express KCNN3 (SK3), the marker of PDGFRA+ interstitial cells of the muscularis, and sit inside the muscle next to the ICC.
edits.evidence: IL11 0%, INHBA 4%, FAP 13%; KCNN3 29% vs 4%, TNC 61% vs 21%, TDO2 29% vs 6%; distance to muscle median 31 µm; top neighbour ICC

edits.reason: Name the type by its location and markers instead of an inflammatory state the data does not show.
edits.evidence: distance to muscle median 31 µm; inflammatory markers ≤13%

edits.reason: No FDC cluster was found. CLU is broadly expressed (14,326 cells), so this type would only draw stray cells.
edits.evidence: FDCSP in 168 cells (23 with 2+ transcripts); type not found

edits.reason: Pericytes and vascular smooth muscle express MYH11. The negative marker contradicts 70% of the cells.
edits.evidence: MYH11 detected in 70% of pericytes

edits.reason: VWF and PECAM1 are shared with lymphatic EC, and the endothelial group marker already has them.
edits.evidence: VWF 83% vs 72%, PECAM1 92% vs 84% in lymphatic EC

edits.reason: Most cells called Arterial EC are capillaries: their arterial markers are almost absent, and their top genes are the capillary markers CA4 and CD36.
edits.evidence: Arterial EC (2,896 cells, 5% of all): GJA4 6%, HEY1 20%; top genes NOTCH4 65% vs 6%, CD36 43% vs 6%, CA4 15% vs 0%

edits.reason: VWF is not specific between venous and other blood vessel EC. Excluding capillary CA4 keeps venules distinct from the new Capillary EC.
edits.evidence: VWF 87% vs 82%; ACKR1 74% vs 27%

questions: Does this section contain a Peyer's patch or lymphoid follicle? B cells (399) and mature DCs cluster deep (median 110 µm from muscle). If there is one, I would keep M cells (none found yet) and draw the follicle so SI-06/SI-07 can be applied; if not, M cells can be removed.
Is this inflamed tissue (e.g. Crohn's ileitis)? I saw no inflammatory fibroblast signature, so I proposed renaming that type to Muscularis fibroblasts; tell me if you want an inflammatory state kept.

You accepted the niche names, and they now show in the legend for every slice in the project.

| Niche | Name | Make-up and where it sits on the H&E |

| N1 | **muscularis** | 51% smooth muscle with fibroblasts and pericytes. It forms the thick muscle bands at the bottom (rows T–AA) and the muscle band under the mucosa (rows J–L). |
| N2 | **submucosa** | Capillaries, submucosal fibroblasts, pericytes and macrophages. It fills the loose tissue around the large vessels (rows L–S). |
| N3 | **lamina propria** | Crypt-top fibroblasts, capillaries and T cells, within about 25 µm of the epithelium. These are the cores of the villi and the tissue between the crypts. |
| N4 | **villus epithelium** | 84% enterocytes. It is the surface lining of the villi in the top-left area. |
| N5 | **crypts** | Cycling TAs (52%), enteroendocrine and goblet cells, with high OLFM4. These are the round crypt profiles in the top-right area and the base of the mucosa. |
| N6 | **goblet-rich crypt epithelium** | Only 12 cells, with high ITLN1, RETNLB and REP15. |
| N7 | **colonic crypt epithelium** | No cells in this slice. The name comes only from its gene program (CD24, SLC26A2, SELENBP1), likely from the other slice (167799). |
| N8 | **colonic surface epithelium** | No cells in this slice. The name comes only from its gene program (SLC26A3, CEACAM5/7), likely from the other slice (167799). |

I wrote the rule for your one Colon prior and changed nothing else:

- **U-1:** kind=region, types=[Paneth cells], regions=[mucosa], mode=exclude, strength=strong. In words: no cell in the mucosa may be called a Paneth cell.

1. **Why only the mucosa:** Paneth cells are epithelial, and epithelium lies only in the mucosa, so excluding them there covers the whole section.
2. **Why strong:** your statement is firm, so I followed it rather than the built-in prior COL-05. COL-05 advises a weak exclusion only, because Paneth cell metaplasia is common in the distal colon in IBD and other chronic colitis. If this tissue might be inflamed, I can lower the rule to weak.
3. **Name not checked:** I couldn't check the name "Paneth cells" against the vocabulary because no annotation was active when I tried. It is the name used in the small-intestine list I drafted earlier.
4. **Colon list:** "Paneth cells" is not in the built-in colon list, so the rule only acts on a colon annotation whose marker list includes that type.

c14_review_annotation.text:
I reviewed version 1 of the sigmoid colon sample (167799), since that is what the app now shows, not the ileum (147328).

1. **Review candidates:** I hid all three candidate areas. On the H&E, A1, A2 and A3 are walls of muscular blood vessels, so smooth muscle there is expected. Of the 21 marker checks I kept 12 as real problems and hid 9 as low detection of types that other markers support.
2. **Main problem:** this colon was annotated with the small-intestine list. 9,064 "Cycling TAs" (22%) are mostly not cycling: only 1,121 express MKI67/TOP2A, and one group of 1,410 are colonocytes (SLC26A3, CA1). The 3,353 "BEST4+ enterocytes" are mostly mature colonocytes (CEACAM7, AQP8; BEST4 in only 10%), and only 79 goblet cells were found. "Capillary EC" also contains venules (ACKR1, about 1,650 cells) and arterial EC (HEY1, 843). Two taxonomy advice items cover these: a colon marker list without Enterocytes, Paneth cells (your U-1) and M cells, and a split of the blood vessel cells.
3. **Context and QC:** the cell types sit where the colon priors expect (stem cells at the crypt base, plasma cells in the lamina propria, ICC and neurons in the muscle), and registration is fine (max offset 5.2 µm). I kept one context advice item: draw the mucosa (the outline fits the H&E) so COL-01 and your U-1 can act. I dropped three drafts: the gd T cells called NK (only 20 cells), epithelial transcript spillover (it doesn't change the calls) and registration (nothing to do).

c16_biology.text: Is there anything biologically interesting in these two sections that I should look at?

Yes, a few things look worth a look. These are leads from the reviews so far, not tested findings. Both sections are labelled "Non-IBD controls (Diverticulitis)", so some local inflammation would fit.

**Sigmoid colon (167799)**
- **An interferon patch in the epithelium.** About 240 epithelial cells (part of the "BEST4+ enterocytes") express RSAD2, IFIT1, DDX58 and IFIH1 in 90–100% of cells. They sit together in one place: they neighbour each other 11 times more often than chance, the most clustered group in the section. A tight patch like this suggests a local event, such as a viral response or an inflamed spot near a diverticulum, rather than noise. The small "Enterocytes" group shares the signal (ISG15, RSAD2), and some of its cells may be the same patch. Checking this group on the H&E is the first thing I would do.
- **NOS2 in the crypt base.** NOS2 is detected in 60% of stem cells and in 40% of one crypt sub-group, against 7–10% elsewhere. Epithelium usually switches NOS2 on in response to IFN-γ, so this could be the same inflammatory signal reaching the stem cell zone.
- **Cycling dendritic cells.** 45% of cDC1 express MKI67/TOP2A. That is unusual and could mean local DC proliferation, or cycling cells mixed into the type.
- **Many glia (4.4% of cells) and many LYVE1+ macrophages (88%).** This fits the large submucosa in this section, with nerve plexuses and macrophages around vessels.

**Terminal ileum (147328)**
- **A possible lymphoid follicle or Peyer's patch.** On the H&E there is a dense basophilic patch under the crypts on the left (rows J–K). B cells, mature DCs (LAMP3+, CCR7+), Tregs and the few naive T cells are each other's nearest neighbours. That looks like an organised immune site, with mature DCs next to Tregs, typical of the follicle T-cell zone. No M cells or follicular dendritic cells were found, which is probably a panel limit.
- **The crypt base, as you described it.** In version 1, stem cells and Paneth cells sat together, with neighbour enrichment of log2 3.7. But the current annotation finds no stem or Paneth cells, and enteroendocrine cells grew from about 500 to 2,181. That jump is more likely mislabelled crypt-base cells than biology.

The whole-section, tile-level view didn't show any obvious tissue damage, but I didn't zoom into the H&E of either suspected spot. Should I show the interferon patch and the ileal follicle on the H&E, and compare the patch's genes with the rest of the epithelium?
